summary: Plumas summit lookout built in 1933; its cab and 20-foot tower were re-erected on Pike County Peak in 1983, where they stand.

facts.design: National Plan CL-100 cab on a 20-foot steel tower (replacement built 1961 or 1962); moved to Pike County Peak in 1983
facts.status_note: The cab and 20-foot tower were dismantled in 1983 and re-erected on Pike County Peak in Yuba County.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest

corrections.why: The cab and tower were moved to Pike County Peak in 1983 and stand there; the Lexington Hill site itself has no lookout structure. For editor review.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1983 appears in the register, the NHLR Pike County Peak entry and the local history; Peakbagging gives 1984. The 1983 date has the most support.

notes_for_editor: Record says gone; the cab and tower were moved to Pike County Peak (us-ca-pike-county-peak, researched separately), so relocated fits. Replacement year: register 1961, June 1962 newspaper announced construction; both kept. Move year: 1983 (register, NHLR, local history) vs 1984 (Peakbagging). Size: 1949 survey gives 14 ft square and 26 ft high; the register's 1933 wording is a 10 enclosed timber tower; not reconciled. The Peakbagging text is a 2006 photo caption page. No source describes the Lexington Hill summit today. Confidence medium.
